title: Bluedip: fill a restaurant's quiet hours
about: A founder describes Bluedip, an app that predicts a restaurant's footfall and revenue hour by hour and estimates what an offer will really do before the owner runs it. Cynqra proposes three cofounders: a CTO, a Chief Product Officer and a CFO. Each builds the team for its area: the CTO a Data Scientist, a Backend Engineer, a Frontend Engineer, DevOps and QA; the CPO a Project Manager, a Designer, a Market Analyst and a Restaurant Revenue Management Specialist; the CFO a Legal and Compliance Advisor. Cofounders hand out their team's work, answer its doubts and review it before it counts. The platform backtests the forecast (its first version fails), the CPO sends the screen design back because it hid the margin, a test catches the ignored cap, the CEO decides one rule on discounts, and the app goes live. The owner's own example, 50% off for 15 customers from 1 to 4 pm, turns out to raise revenue and lose money; Bluedip recommends the offer that earns it.
note: Prepared script for demo mode. Every word a worker says in demo mode comes from this file, and the product shows that. The models and the app in files/ are real: they are tested, backtested and deployed for real.
messy: I want to build Bluedip, an app that helps restaurant owners fill their quiet hours. It should predict footfall and revenue for breakfast, lunch and dinner in real time, recommend offers for the slow periods, and let an owner create a limited-time offer, like 50% off for at most 15 customers between 1 PM and 4 PM, and see how many customers it will bring and what it does to revenue. First release for restaurant owners only: no diner app and no payments.

objective.product: Bluedip: an app that helps restaurant owners fill their quiet hours with offers that earn money
objective.target_customer: Owners of independent restaurants and small chains in Indian cities
objective.primary_outcome: Owners see expected footfall and revenue for every hour and meal, and run offers that fill quiet hours without losing margin
objective.business_outcome: Restaurants pay a monthly subscription because Bluedip adds more margin than it costs
objective.success_criteria: A live app that predicts footfall and revenue by hour and estimates the customers, revenue and margin an offer brings, and a checked business plan
objective.constraints: No diner-facing app or payments in the first release; every estimate shows the assumptions behind it
objective.priorities: Honest estimates first, then recommendations for each meal, then growth

outcomes: Owners see their day's footfall and revenue before it happens
Every offer is estimated, in customers, revenue and margin, before it runs
Restaurants pay for Bluedip because it adds more than it costs

workforce.summary: Bluedip is a business built on prediction and on money. It needs a CTO to build and run the product and its models, a Chief Product Officer so restaurant owners find it useful, and a CFO because its whole value is whether an offer earns or loses money. No Chief Compliance Officer: release 1 takes no payments and holds no diner data. Each cofounder chose the team for its own area.

cofounders.why: Bluedip is an app built on prediction models: someone must own how it is built, checked and put live.
Restaurant owners must find it useful between services: someone must own who it is for and what it must do for them.
The whole value is money: whether an offer earns or loses, the price owners pay and the funding Bluedip needs.

CTO.summary: The product is its predictions and the app built on them. A Data Scientist for the models, a Backend Engineer for the demand and offer engine, a Frontend Engineer for the owner's app, QA for the acceptance tests, and DevOps to put it live and keep it running.

roles.why: Bluedip is its predictions: the footfall forecast, the offer estimate, and how both learn.
The demand and offer engine behind every number the owner sees, and the cap that must hold.
The one screen the owner uses, and the web server behind it.
Every acceptance check becomes a test that runs on every change.
Puts Bluedip live on the company's own host with a health check and a way back.

CPO.summary: Owners must trust the numbers and act on them in a minute. A Project Manager to plan the work and write the spec, a Designer for the owner's screen, a Market Analyst for who pays and how to reach them, and a Restaurant Revenue Management Specialist for when a discount earns money.

roles.why: Plans the roadmap and writes the app's spec and acceptance checks.
One screen an owner reads standing up: what it shows first decides whether they trust it.
Who pays, what they use today, and how to reach the first restaurants.

roles.why: Knows when a discount earns money and when it only gives it away: the core of every recommendation.

CFO.summary: Offers touch advertising, data and tax rules. A Legal and Compliance Advisor keeps the register of what applies and what a lawyer must confirm.

roles.why: Offers must not mislead diners, and data and tax rules apply to every offer.

t_08.problem: Owners will set their own discounts. A deep one can fill the room and still lose money, because customers who would have come anyway pay less too; an app that lets that happen without saying so loses the owner's trust.
t_08.recommendation: No offer deeper than 50%, and none that takes the bill below its food cost. Every offer shows its margin change after food cost before it is created, and a better offer when there is one.
t_08.cost: some owners will want deeper discounts than Bluedip allows
t_08.what_would_change_this: Pilot results showing offers deeper than 50% adding margin in some restaurants.

t_11.acceptance_check: Use 35% of the average bill as the food cost until the owner enters their own, and show it on screen as an assumption, next to every margin figure. Ask for the real figure on first use. Never hide it: a margin figure is only as good as its food cost.
